In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

self-determination theory is an empirically supported theory of motivation that provides a framework to understand the role of intrinsic motivation and autonomous extrinsic motivation in educational settings and to design interventions that support students' and educators' psychological need satisfaction.
SDT is the most complete theory of motivation to date and has been shown to have a significant impact on the educational system.
SDT has provided a rich and robust theory of motivation that has been applied to many areas of psychology and education and has generated a substantial body of research.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SDT is an empirically supported framework for understanding the nature and nurture of human motivation in educational settings.

intrinsic motivation is the ultimate goal, extrinsic motivation can be beneficial if it is autonomous, and both intrinsic and autonomous forms of motivation are facilitated by supports for basic psychological needs.

intrinsic motivation is the most desirable form of motivation, but that autonomous forms of extrinsic motivations are also desirable, and that both are enhanced by the satisfaction of students' basic psychological need for autonomy, competence and relatedness.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the most effective motivational strategies for students and teachers are those that support the fulfillment of their basic psychological needs.

SDT provides a framework for understanding and promoting the conditions that support students and teachers in developing and sustaining the intrinsic and autonomous forms of motivation that are so critical for optimal educational experiences.
the quality of motivation is more important than the quantity of motivation in understanding the effects of motivation on learning and well being.
